chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abi Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And give their due on the day of its harvest.'

They all said. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from the zakat. He gives the poor person a handful after a handful, and from the leftover stalks a handful after a handful, until he finishes. And he leaves for the guardian a known wage. And he leaves from the palm trees a 'mi'farrah' and an 'umm Ju'urr', and he leaves for the guardian, which is in the enclosure, the 'adhq' (date clusters), two 'adhqs', and three, for their protection.'

ai.seo_question: How is agricultural zakat distributed according to the explanation of the verse 'And give their due on the day of its harvest'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse 'And give its due on the day of its harvest' (Quran 6:141) by defining the specific mechanics of agricultural zakat, emphasizing the obligation to distribute produce to the poor in small portions until exhausted. The narration further details the exemptions and wages for the crop guardian, including retaining specific palm varieties and fruit clusters, thereby establishing a comprehensive legal framework for landowners in Shia jurisprudence.
